# Markdown Best Practices

## Headings
- Use ATX-style headings (# ## ###) consistently
- Start with H1 (#) for main title, then H2, etc.
- Leave a blank line before and after headings

## Links
- Use reference-style links for better readability: [text][ref]
- Define references at the bottom of the document
- Use descriptive link text, avoid "click here"

## Code
- Use fenced code blocks with language specification
- Indent inline code with backticks
- Use syntax highlighting where possible

## Lists
- Use consistent indentation (4 spaces)
- Add blank lines between list items for readability
- Use numbered lists for sequential steps

## Tables
- Use pipe tables for simple tables
- Align columns properly with colons
- Keep tables simple and readable

## Images
- Use descriptive alt text
- Store images in appropriate directories
- Use relative paths for local images

## Formatting
- Use italics for emphasis, bold for strong emphasis
- Avoid excessive formatting
- Use blockquotes for quotes or highlights

## Structure
- Keep lines under 80 characters where possible
- Use blank lines to separate sections
- Front matter for metadata when needed
